image_description: A side-front view of a vintage-style minibus parked on a paved street. The vehicle has a two-tone color scheme (beige/cream lower, white upper) with red and black graphics. It features a boxy body, large windshield, side windows, and visible wheels. There is text on the front destination board and side panels. A tripod stand is visible in the foreground left.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The vehicle exhibits a distinct boxy silhouette typical of minibuses. Its length is visibly shorter than a standard city bus, and the roof height suggests adequate interior headroom.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Large windshield and row of side windows along passenger area.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A large, split-pane windshield is clearly visible at the front. A continuous row of rectangular side windows runs along the passenger compartment.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Height is substantial, with entrance door at front or mid-body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The vehicle has significant height relative to its width. A door frame and handle mechanism are visible behind the front wheel arch, indicating a front/mid-body entrance.
The vertical seam and track structure near the front wheel suggest a sliding door mechanism, consistent with minibus designs.
There is a distinct hood/bonnet section ahead of the windshield and driver's cabin, indicating a front-engine layout.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rear of the vehicle is occluded by the viewing angle; only the side and front are visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bus features a specific livery with beige, white, and red colors, along with graphic stripes and text, fitting the description of company/route markings.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Standard van-sized wheels with steel or alloy rims.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible wheels are proportional to a light commercial vehicle/minibus size, with dark rims that appear to be steel or simple alloy.
Based on the number of side windows (approx. 3-4 visible on this side) and overall dimensions, the capacity aligns with the 4-10 passenger range typical for this class.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The rear wheel arch geometry seems slightly inconsistent with the front. The contact patch of the front tire with the ground is slightly ambiguous, lacking a sharp shadow line, giving a slight 'floating' impression.
Reflections in the side windows are overly uniform and painterly, lacking the crisp environmental details expected in a real photograph of a glossy surface.
